title: Currently making a TCG, how do you guys approach UI + art assets when you suck at design?
author: Illustrious_Sleep723
selftext:
I'm a software engineer building my own TCG, and I'm running into a problem I suspect a lot of solo devs have: I can build the actual game, but I'm absolutely terrible at visual design.

I'm using Claude quite heavily for the programming side, and it's been great for implementing mechanics, screens, data structures, etc. bbut when it comes to things like: UI panels and buttons, Icons, Backgrounds, Effects, Fonts/typography, general visual identity …I have basically no idea what I'm doing.

So I'm curious how other solo developers approach this.

If you were a software engineer with basically zero design/art skills building a TCG, what would your workflow be? I'm using Unity. Thanks in advance! :)

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body: When I truly have no idea the direction I'm looking for I have Claude do 10 unique mockups of the UI/asset I'm looking to generate. That usually gives me enough of an idea where then I can say "oh #4 is the right direction, make 5 more variants of #4" and then keep iterating

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: Always, always have Claude create multiple versions for review. I've never regretted doing it and I typically do end up merging parts of each.

comments.author: IriFlina
comments.body:
Use inspiration from existing game uis, feed it to claude, use figma + figma mcp or an alternative like penpot + mcp to make claude mock up the ui. If something isn’t to your liking tell claude to change it or give you variants on the ui you can choose from. 

If your game has a theme tell claude to make the ui more “diegetic” and give you multiple options to choose from.

comments.author: R3DB71ND
comments.body:
You can provide Claude images or URLs of UI that you like. Put it all in a folder and ask Calude to refer to it. Once you start getting close to a syle you like, tell Claude to make detailed notes that it should refer to when generating UI. In real life this is called a style guide or mood board. Basically interact with Claude as if it were a real designer that you hired.  
  
Describe what the user needs to go, instead of giving it detailed instructions, "as a X person, I need to do Y, because Z." In software development we call this a user story. For example: "Propose a UI that meets this user story: As a player of the game I need a way to cycle through weapon inventory quickly so the the flow of the battle is not interupted. Refer to the style guide and mood board folder." Again, talk to it like a professional UI designer.

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: If it’s 2d I mostly use spritelab , pixel lab , sprite cook
